boundary_note: Stralsund 15 July–20 August; September Rügen convention is later context, not an extension of the frozen battle. Tactical and campaign replacement boundaries are unset; phases are research hypotheses. No feature admission or historical rating fit.

claims.value: Bodart: side A about 40,000 under Brune; side B Swedish defenders under Peyron; people count absent.
claims.rationale: Read on the registered page image. His general rule is forces disposable for the engagement, rounded upward (shared research-conventions index); a stated siege endpoint or engaged subset takes precedence over treating it as an opening count. Population/timing alternatives are not reconciled. English rendering (ours): "The French, about 40,000 under Marshal Brune, compel the Swedish garrison under Major-General Peyron to surrender the place. Most of the garrison had already escaped to Rügen. The French captured 500 guns."

claims.value: Napoleon’s 22 July disposition projects 34,000 infantry and 4,000 cavalry, 38,000 total, for Brune’s army.
claims.rationale: Linearized table totals from the image; planned composition, not a verified simultaneous siege return. Bodart’s about 40,000 differs in timing/scope. English rendering (ours): "Infantry 34,000, cavalry 4,000; total 38,000." English rendering of heading (ours): "To Marshal Berthier, Dresden, 22 July 1807."

claims.value: Key-Åberg distinguishes a secret convention ceiling of 14,000 for the Swedish field army from an apparent 16,000 implied by comparing public treaty terms; neither is an actual Stralsund garrison return.
claims.rationale: Treaty obligations and planned Finnish reinforcements; actual siege defender number remains unknown. English rendering (ours): "should be raised to a higher strength than 14,000 men" English rendering (ours): "ought to amount to 16,000 men."

citations.quote: skulle uppbringas till högre numerär än 14,000 man

claims.value: Napoleon instructs Berthier to put Chasseloup over engineering and Brune to use Reille for capitulation discussions.
claims.rationale: Order 12936 begins on p 436 with 22 July dateline. Intended appointments, not proof of execution; Brune superior siege authority remains distinct. English rendering (ours): "Order General Chasseloup to take command of the engineers there." English rendering (ours): "he is to employ General Reille, my aide-de-camp."

citations.quote: Ordonnez au général Chasseloup d’y prendre le commandement du génie.
il emploie le général Reille, mon aide de camp.

claims.value: Key-Åberg describes Gustaf IV Adolf’s political refusal of peace and General Toll’s later convention with Brune; these are wider/late authorities, not proof that Peyron directed every phase.
claims.rationale: King, local commandant and later negotiator are separate offices; exact tactical authority transfer remains unknown. English rendering (ours): "Gustaf IV Adolf, as is known, had no thought of making peace with Napoleon" English rendering (ours): "a convention concluded between General Toll and Marshal Brune at Stralsund on 7 September"

citations.quote: hade Gustaf IV Adolf, såsom kändt är, ingen tanke på att ingå fred med Napoléon
en mellan general Toll och marskalk Brune den 7 Sept. i Stralsund afsluten konvention

claims.value: Key-Åberg says the Swedish border defenders alone faced the July advance, while Blücher’s Prussians were inactive after peace and British auxiliaries stayed on Rügen.
claims.rationale: Narrative participation distinction; do not add treaty allies to siege defender headcount. English rendering (ours): "whose borders were defended solely by the Swedish troops." English rendering (ours): "the British auxiliary troops prudently kept out of danger on Rügen."

citations.quote: hvars gränser försvarades endast och allenast af de svenska trupperna.
de engelska hjelptrupperna höllo sig försigtigtvis utom all fara på ön Rügen.

claims.value: The Swedish army was driven within Stralsund’s walls by the evening of 14 July.
claims.rationale: English rendering (ours): "On the evening of 14 July the Swedish army had been driven back within Stralsund’s walls"

claims.value: Napoleon orders sufficient artillery for three simultaneous attacks.
claims.rationale: English rendering (ours): "so that three attacks can be made at once and this place quickly taken."

claims.value: Key-Åberg describes Swedish evacuation of Stralsund, then Rügen under the September convention permitting return to Sweden.
claims.rationale: Fortress loss, later island evacuation and survival of the army are separate outcomes. English rendering (ours): "the Swedes evacuated Stralsund and soon afterwards also the island of Rügen" English rendering (ours): "was allowed to return unhindered to Sweden."
